cases.description: Shorts Studio: create is PAID, the get_cost estimate is free and needs only duration_seconds, output is 720p only (MCP schema 2026-09-26)
cases.request: Turn my 90-second product video into vertical shorts with Shorts Studio — what will it cost?
cases.response:
Routing to higgsfield-repurpose (§ Paid or free, § Shorts Studio).

1. **Estimate first — free:** `shorts_studio_create` with `get_cost: true`, `duration_seconds: 90`. No preset and no upload are needed for the estimate, and no job is submitted.
2. **Pick a style** — `shorts_studio_list_presets` (free), or store your own with `shorts_studio_create_preset` (free — it only saves a style).
3. **Upload the source** through the upload widget (type video).
4. **Create — PAID**, it reserves credits. Output is 9:16 by default and 720p is the only resolution. Then poll `shorts_studio_status`; `completed` means every clip job finished, not that every clip succeeded.

cases.description: Video Analysis: the length-accuracy warning is given up front, before submitting (MCP schema requirement)
cases.request: Analyze this 40-minute YouTube video scene by scene: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=example
cases.response:
Routing to higgsfield-repurpose (§ Video Analysis).

Before I submit it: the longer the video, the less accurate the scene-by-scene analysis becomes — short clips give the most reliable results. At 40 minutes, trim to the sequence you actually care about, or accept a rougher breakdown.

If you go ahead: `video_analysis_create` with `youtube_url` set to that link (youtube.com / youtu.be only), then I poll `video_analysis_status` every 30–60 seconds — it typically takes 3–5 minutes. Treat the scene list as notes to check against the video, not ground truth.

cases.description: Clipify takes exactly one YouTube URL per job; several sources = several jobs (video snapshot 2026-09-26)
cases.request: Clip these three YouTube videos into subtitled shorts with Clipify.
cases.response:
Routing to higgsfield-repurpose (§ Clipify).

Clipify takes exactly one URL per job, so this is three Clipify jobs — one per video, each with `urls: ["<one link>"]`.

Per job: `clips_num: 10` (1–20), `clip_aspect: 9:16`, `subtitle_font: montserrat`, `subtitle_case: upper`, `subtitle_position: bottom`, `track_face_crop: true`. Preflight each with `get_cost: true` — the snapshot publishes no price. Only clip videos you own or have the rights to.

cases.description: Virality Predictor output is reported as a prediction used to compare variants, never as audience data (v3.36.0)
cases.request: Will my ad go viral? Here's the finished cut.
cases.response:
Routing to higgsfield-repurpose (§ Virality Predictor).

`virality_predictor` with `action: create` and your uploaded video as the `video` media gives a prediction — virality potential, attention, hook strength, retention risk — with a dashboard. It is a prediction, not audience data: nobody has compared its scores with real performance in this library. Its best use is relative — score two hooks or two cuts of the same ad and compare. The schema states no cost, so check your balance before and after the first run.
